name: Reasoning and Behavior
summary: Executive functions, cognitive control, and how the brain produces purposeful behavior.

sections.heading: Executive Functions
sections.content: Working memory holds and manipulates information (dorsolateral PFC). Cognitive flexibility allows switching between tasks and mental frameworks. Inhibitory control suppresses inappropriate impulses and distractions. Planning sequences steps to achieve a goal. Monitoring evaluates performance and adjusts strategies.

sections.heading: The Default Mode Network
sections.content: When not focused on external tasks, the brain enters a default mode — a network of brain regions (medial PFC, posterior cingulate, angular gyrus) that activates during daydreaming, self-reflection, mental time travel, and imagining others' perspectives.

sections.heading: Cognitive Biases
sections.content: The brain uses mental shortcuts (heuristics) to make quick decisions. While often useful, these can lead to systematic errors: confirmation bias (seeking information that confirms existing beliefs), anchoring (over-relying on the first piece of information), and availability heuristic (judging probability by how easily examples come to mind).
